import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Stochastic_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 7  # destinations
    S = 12  # scenarios
    alpha = 0.9  # confidence level
    max_violations = int(math.floor((1 - alpha) * S))

    supplies = [101, 91, 146, 193, 134]
    recourse_caps = [40, 36, 58, 77, 53]
    base_costs = [[6.7, 20.76, 8.46, 13.65, 6.8, 12.55, 11.35], [10.81, 7.11, 19.02, 12.3, 17.48, 10.93, 14.15], [7.66, 6.68, 16.26, 21.4, 16.95, 13.12, 23.88], [11.54, 10.6, 5.08, 23.74, 13.76, 16.5, 21.95], [14.44, 12.88, 16.17, 21.15, 9.83, 7.53, 10.86]]
    recourse_costs = [[13.4, 41.52, 16.92, 27.3, 13.6, 25.1, 22.7], [21.62, 14.22, 38.04, 24.6, 34.96, 21.86, 28.3], [15.32, 13.36, 32.52, 42.8, 33.9, 26.24, 47.76], [23.08, 21.2, 10.16, 47.48, 27.52, 33.0, 43.9], [28.88, 25.76, 32.34, 42.3, 19.66, 15.06, 21.72]]
    demand_scenarios = [[32, 26, 35, 46, 24, 14, 18], [41, 31, 30, 31, 20, 11, 19], [31, 32, 29, 31, 14, 14, 15], [29, 24, 38, 29, 20, 12, 27], [32, 38, 25, 34, 24, 11, 18], [33, 37, 39, 29, 18, 10, 24], [40, 36, 41, 36, 22, 13, 25], [40, 30, 39, 33, 16, 13, 15], [32, 24, 34, 38, 20, 15, 21], [37, 24, 42, 42, 25, 14, 24], [39, 24, 29, 49, 21, 10, 18], [33, 28, 39, 33, 14, 9, 24]]

    # Big-M: largest demand * 2
    M = max(demand_scenarios[s][j] for s in range(S) for j in range(J)) * 2

    # --- Variables ---
    # Stage 1: base shipments
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Base_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Stage 2: recourse shipments per scenario
    y = {}
    for s in range(S):
        for i in range(I):
            for j in range(J):
                y[(i,j,s)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Recourse_S{i}_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # Violation indicators
    z = {}
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            z[(j,s)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Violate_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # --- Objective: minimize base cost + expected recourse cost ---
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(base_costs[i][j] * x[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J))
        + (1.0 / S) * quicksum(recourse_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j,s)]
                               for s in range(S) for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply (base)
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"SupplyBase_S{i}")

    # C2: Supply (recourse per scenario)
    for i in range(I):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(y[(i,j,s)] for j in range(J)) <= recourse_caps[i],
                name=f"SupplyRecourse_S{i}_Sc{s}")

    # C3: Demand chance constraint (SAA)
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(x[(i,j)] + y[(i,j,s)] for i in range(I))
                + M * z[(j,s)] >= demand_scenarios[s][j],
                name=f"DemandChance_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # C4: Violation budget per destination
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(z[(j,s)] for s in range(S)) <= max_violations,
            name=f"ViolationBudget_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

Subject: Two-stage shipping plan to meet store demand reliably under forecast uncertainty

To: Retail Operations and Logistics Leadership
From: Supply Chain Director

Challenge
Customer demand across stores fluctuates from week to week, and our lead times, carrier commitments, and warehouse picking schedules require us to set shipments before demand is fully known. If we ship too little, we risk stockouts, lost sales, and customer dissatisfaction. If we ship too much, we tie up working capital and incur avoidable handling and transfer costs. We need a practical way to protect service while controlling spend under this uncertainty.

Two-phase approach
We will operate with a two-stage plan. First, we will lock a base shipping plan from each warehouse to each store before demand is realized. This base plan will respect available inventory at each warehouse and leverage our standard, lower-cost lanes. Second, after demand is observed, we will make targeted emergency shipments to cover any shortfalls. These emergency moves carry higher unit costs and are limited by the capacity we can credibly secure in short order. Emergency shipments are strictly a backstop and will not be used to pre-position speculative stock.

Reliability target
Our service commitment is to meet each store’s full demand in at least a defined confidence level of forecast scenarios. It is acceptable to miss demand in a small share of scenarios when the outcomes are especially extreme, but not as a routine. This strikes the right balance between dependable on-shelf availability and prudent use of working capital and freight budget. We will test the base plan against the scenario set and confirm that each store meets the service requirement across the vast majority of forecasted outcomes.

Cost focus
Our financial focus is the total expected cost across the forecast scenarios: base shipping spend plus the average emergency shipping spend. The base plan should shoulder the predictable portion of demand on cost-effective lanes without overcommitting inventory, while the emergency plan should efficiently cover residual volatility without breaching capacity or inflating spend. We will evaluate trade-offs between investing more in the base plan (to reduce later emergency costs) and holding more flexibility for emergency moves (to avoid overstock), always within our service and capacity guardrails.

Operating guardrails
- Base shipments cannot exceed available inventory at each warehouse for the planning window.
- Emergency shipments cannot exceed the separately secured short-notice capacity by warehouse and mode.
- Emergency shipments are deployed only to close gaps to store demand after actuals are known.
- The scenario set will be reviewed regularly to ensure it reflects the latest demand signals and seasonality.
- We will monitor store-level service coverage (percentage of scenarios fully met), base and emergency capacity utilization, and total expected cost.

Next steps
1) Confirm the scenario set and service target with Commercial and Finance; refresh forecasts and review any store-level outliers.
2) Build the base plan by lane and warehouse within available inventory and standard lead times; identify lanes most sensitive to uncertainty.
3) Secure emergency capacity and rate cards; define lane-specific triggers for emergency releases after demand is observed.
4) Run scenario evaluations to confirm store-level service coverage and quantify expected base and emergency spend; iterate the base plan as needed to improve cost-service balance.
5) Implement weekly governance: pre-commit base volumes, then execute emergency moves against actuals; publish service coverage and cost results to stakeholders.
